transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Lindqvist, thank you for coming back to see me. I need to talk to you about your discharge papers.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope this is fast. I spent three hours on the phone this morning.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry. I made a mistake with your follow-up care. I gave you a clinic that does not take your insurance.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are joking.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am not. I sent you to a place that you cannot use. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It makes sense that you failed. I was a paramedic for twelve years. I know how discharge checklists work. This is a basic failure.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is. I take full responsibility for this. I am truly sorry for the stress this has caused you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stress? I have a condition that needs monitoring now. I can't just wait for you to find a map.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Do you understand how the insurance mismatch happened, or should I explain it further?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I understand perfectly. You didn't check the provider network.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. I did not check the network. I apologize.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My wife is furious. I am furious. I trusted the team here to handle the transition.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you are angry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Angry is a very small word for this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? I have no appointment. I have no doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am working on a solution.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a solution. Which doctor? When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am looking into some options right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Give me a name. Give me a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I don't have the name of the new clinic yet.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. I am sitting here and you have nothing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry. I am trying to fix it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are trying. I am the one without care. Who is actually taking ownership of this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am. I am the one who made the error, and I am the one who will fix it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You keep saying sorry. Sorry doesn't get me into a clinic.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it doesn't.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know why this happened. Was the system down? Were you rushed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No. I simply did not verify the insurance. There is no excuse for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: At least you aren't lying about it. But I'm still without a doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you actually understand? I know the clinical path for my recovery. If I miss this window, I'm back in a hospital bed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear your concern about the timing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop saying you hear me. Tell me what happens next.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will send you an email.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An email? When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sometime today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Today is not a time. Do you mean by noon? By five?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not sure. I have to call around.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is a joke. You make a mistake, and then you give me a vague promise.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will do my best to find a clinic.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Your best wasn't good enough on the paperwork, and it isn't good enough now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want a written guarantee that the next place takes my insurance.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will try to get that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Try? Or will you do it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will see what I can do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am done with this conversation. I'll be waiting for that email.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will send it as soon as I can.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts the patient and remains regulated and calm despite significant pushback and anger.

E.justification: The error is named in the second turn, lay language is used, and comprehension is checked twice ('Does that make sense?' and 'Do you understand... or should I explain it further?').

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language multiple times, takes full personal responsibility, and maintains this accountability throughout the encounter.

R.justification: The resident names a specific emotion ('I can see that you are angry') and engages with the patient's distress, though relies on generic validation ('I understand', 'I hear you') for other bids.

T.justification: The plan is vague ('I will send you an email'), lacks a specific timeline ('Sometime today'), and does not address prevention or the patient's role.
